title: Étale-local integral monodromy and exact rational realization
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $A=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For a scheme $T$, use the continuous-function coefficient sheaves $A_T$ and $E_T$ of [def-weil-pbc-lisse-lattice-coefficients]; modules mean sheaf modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] on $T_{\mathrm{proét}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. A module is lisse if it is pro-étale locally free of finite rank, with rank zero allowed.

For every connected quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme $T$ with Noetherian underlying topological space (every ascending chain of open subsets stabilizes) and geometric point $\bar t$, put $\Pi_T=\pi_1(T,\bar t)$, the profinite étale fundamental group of [def-galois-fibre-functor]. Let $\operatorname{Rep}^{\mathrm{cont}}_E(\Pi_T)$ have as objects finite-dimensional $E$-vector spaces $V$ with jointly continuous $E$-linear $\Pi_T$-action, with the usual finite-dimensional $\ell$-adic topology; its morphisms are equivariant $E$-linear maps. There is an $E$-linear fully faithful functor
$$J_T:\operatorname{Rep}^{\mathrm{cont}}_E(\Pi_T)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Mod}(T_{\mathrm{proét}},E_T).$$
Its values are lisse. It sends every short exact sequence of representations whose underlying sequence of $E$-vector spaces is exact to a short exact sequence in the ambient sheaf-module category. Its normalization on an invariant finite free $A$-lattice $B\subset V$ is
$$J_T(V)\cong\left(\varprojlim_{n\ge1}\nu^*\mathcal L(B/\varpi^nB)\right)[1/\ell],$$
where $\nu:T_{\mathrm{proét}}\to T_{\mathrm{ét}}$ and its module inverse image $\nu^*$ are the site-comparison morphism and inverse image of [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], and $\mathcal L(B/\varpi^nB)$ is the finite locally constant étale sheaf corresponding to the finite discrete continuous $\Pi_T$-module $B/\varpi^nB$ under [cor-galois-lisse-representations](1). Here an invariant finite free lattice means a $\Pi_T$-stable finite free $A$-submodule $B$ with $E\otimes_A B\cong V$. The isomorphisms are compatible with equivariant maps, independently of the invariant lattice. In particular the functor is the integral-monodromy realization followed by inversion of $\ell$, rather than a choice of unrelated realizations.

Let $S$ be any scheme [def-pc-scheme] with Noetherian underlying topological space. For every finite diagram $(L_a,f_b)$ of lisse $E_S$-modules (a finite list of objects and morphisms with specified sources and targets) there is an étale covering family $u_i:T_i\to S$ by connected qcqs schemes with Noetherian underlying topological space, geometric points $\bar t_i$, and finite diagrams $(V_{a,i},h_{b,i})$ in $\operatorname{Rep}^{\mathrm{cont}}_E(\Pi_{T_i})$ with isomorphisms $J_{T_i}(V_{a,i})\cong u_i^{-1}L_a$ that identify every $J_{T_i}(h_{b,i})$ with $u_i^{-1}f_b$. An empty base has the empty covering. No invertibility assumption on $\ell$ on $S$, no ring-theoretic Noetherianity and no separation hypothesis on $S$ is imposed.

source.place: Definition 6.8.3, Proposition 6.8.4(1),(4),(6), pp. 59–60, and the integral-monodromy reduction in the proof of Corollary 6.8.5, p. 60. The exact-realization formulation makes the comparison used in that proof explicit; it does not assert closure of all pro-étale lisse sheaves.

proof.text: Integral monodromy, before rationalization. Apply [lem-sfb-integral-lisse-reduction-equivalence] and [det-pe-finite-local-systems-twist] to identify integral lisse $A_T$-modules with compatible towers of finite locally constant etale $A/\varpi^n$-modules, whose reductions are normalized. The finite-ring equivalence [cor-galois-lisse-representations](1), including its compatibility with scalar extension, identifies these with compatible towers of finite discrete continuous $\Pi_T$-modules $B_n$, free over $A/\varpi^n$ of a single rank $r$. Connectedness ensures a single rank. By [lem-pod-adic-limit-finite-modules](1),(2), $B=\varprojlim B_n$ is finite over $A$, has precisely these reductions, and its inverse-limit topology is adic. In fact it is free: choose a basis at level one and recursively lift it to a basis at level $n+1$; a lifted matrix is invertible because its determinant is a unit modulo $\varpi$. The resulting compatible bases identify $B$ with $\varprojlim(A/\varpi^n)^r=A^r$. The coordinate actions make $\Pi_T\times B\to B$ jointly continuous, because their composites with every finite discrete projection are continuous. Conversely a continuous action on finite free $B$ gives those discrete actions. The Hom bijection in the adic-limit lemma, restricted to equivariant maps at every level, proves full faithfulness. Thus there is an equivalence $K_T$ from continuous finite free $A$-representations to integral lisse modules, with $K_T(B)=\varprojlim_n\nu^*\mathcal L(B/\varpi^nB)$, naturally in maps. No use is made of part (2) of the Galois node, whose extra hypotheses are absent here.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(1), with Corollary 5.1.5 as recalled after Definition 6.8.3; integral-monodromy sentence of Corollary 6.8.5

proof.text: Hom after inverting $\ell$. For integral lisse $M,N$ put $H=\mathcal Hom_{A_T}(M,N)$ [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. On a common trivializing covering this is the sheaf of finite matrices, so $H$ is integral lisse, and the entrywise map gives $H[1/\ell]\cong\mathcal Hom_{E_T}(M[1/\ell],N[1/\ell])$. These local identifications are canonical (a matrix represents the same linear map under change of basis), so glue. Here $A_T[1/\ell]=E_T$ by the integral reduction lemma; for a finite free model, tensoring with this ring equals the colimit of repeated multiplication by $\ell$, and hence this equality holds for all these locally finite free modules. Apply [det-pe-bounded-continuity-sections] with the small filtered index $\mathbf N$, $U=T$, $q=0$, and the complexes $H[0]$ joined by multiplication by $\ell$: the common lower bound is zero and $T$ is qcqs. It gives $H[1/\ell](T)=H(T)[1/\ell]$. Therefore the actual ambient sheaf Hom is $\operatorname{Hom}_{A_T}(M,N)[1/\ell]$. This proves rational full faithfulness of integral lisse modules directly; finite-level full faithfulness alone would not suffice.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(4) and its internal-Hom proof; Lemma 6.8.2

proof.text: Construction of $J_T$ and its canonical normalization. By [lem-pod-profinite-stable-lattice], every finite dimensional continuous $E$-representation has an invariant finite free $A$-lattice $B$. For two such representations with lattices $B,C$, any $E$-linear map is a finite matrix in lattice bases. Multiplication by $\ell^m$ for a sufficiently large $m\geq0$ puts every entry in $A$. Thus every equivariant $E$-map is $\ell^{-m}g$ for an equivariant $A$-map $g:B\to C$, and two presentations agree exactly when they agree after multiplying by a common power of $\ell$. This identifies representation Hom with $\operatorname{Hom}_{A,\Pi_T}(B,C)[1/\ell]$. Combine step 1 with step 2 to define $J_T(V)=K_T(B)[1/\ell]$ and $J_T(\ell^{-m}g)=\ell^{-m}K_T(g)[1/\ell]$. Independence of a fraction, addition, scalar multiplication and composition follow after a common multiplication by $\ell$, where they hold for $K_T$. For two lattices in the same $V$, their finite bases show $\ell^mB\subset C$ and $\ell^mC\subset B$ for some $m$. The identity on $V$ therefore gives a canonical isomorphism of the two realizations by this Hom correspondence; the reverse identity is its inverse. For three choices the comparisons satisfy the cocycle equation because all represent the identity of $V$. They also commute with every equivariant map. Hence a choice of lattices defines an $E$-linear fully faithful functor independent up to these specified natural isomorphisms. Its values are lisse since $K_T(B)$ is locally $A_T^r$ and rationalization is locally $E_T^r$. Step 1 gives exactly the required inverse-limit normalization, including rank zero.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(1),(4), proof of Corollary 6.8.5; stable lattices: Stanford lecture 19, Proposition 1.1.9

proof.text: Compatible lattices for an exact sequence. Given $0\to V'\to V\to V''\to0$, choose an invariant finite free lattice $B\subset V$ by [lem-pod-profinite-stable-lattice]. Put $B'=B\cap V'$ and $B''=\operatorname{im}(B\to V'')$. The ring $A$ is a DVR, hence every ideal is principal and it is Noetherian [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr, def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. In the family of finitely generated submodules of $B'$ a maximal member exists by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finite-module-acc]; adjoining any element of $B'$ shows that member is all of $B'$. Thus $B'$ is finite, and $B''$ is finite as a quotient of $B$. Both are torsion free as submodules of vector spaces, hence finite free by [lem-sc-dvr-fg-torsionfree-free]. Each spans the required vector space: multiply any vector of $V'$ by a sufficiently high power of $\ell$ to enter $B$, and lift any vector of $V''$ to $V$ and do the same. Both actions are continuous: choose an $A$-basis of each lattice and extend its $E$-basis to a basis of its containing vector space; the adic lattice topology is the subspace topology, and the restricted action is continuous. Lift a basis of $B''$ to $B$ to split $0\to B'\to B\to B''\to0$ as $A$-modules; the splitting need not be equivariant. Therefore reduction modulo every $\varpi^n$ is a short exact sequence of finite continuous representations, with surjective transition maps on its kernel tower. Arbitrarily chosen lattices would not give this reduction exactness.

source.place: Integral exactness implicit in proof of Corollary 6.8.5; ordinary module inputs: Stacks Tags 00IK and 0AUW

proof.text: Exact inverse limits in the sheaf category. Apply the exact finite-coefficient equivalence [cor-galois-lisse-representations](1) to the reduced sequences from step 4, then apply the module inverse image $\nu^*$ of [sk-thm-pe-classical-sheaves]. It is exact into the ambient category $\operatorname{Mod}(T_{\mathrm{proét}},A_{n,T})$, not only into the classical subcategory: by [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] it is, on sheaves of modules over the finite discrete ring $A/\varpi^n$, the left adjoint of $\nu_*$ (so it preserves cokernels) and it preserves finite limits (so it preserves kernels). This gives compatible short exact sequences $0\to F'_n\to F_n\to F''_n\to0$ of pro-etale $A_T$-modules, with epimorphic transitions on $F'_n$. Products of these sequences are exact by [det-pe-products-exact]. By [det-pe-milnor-epimorphic] applied to $(F'_n)$, $1-T$ on $\prod F'_n$ is epic. Limits are sectionwise by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful]. Given a section $c$ of $\varprojlim F''_n$, the product epimorphism locally lifts its tuple of coordinates to $b\in\prod F_n$; the defect $(1-T)b$ is a section of $\prod F'_n$. After a further covering it has the form $(1-T)a$ for $a\in\prod F'_n$. Then $b-a$ is compatible and lifts $c$. Both local lifting assertions, and the conclusion that the limit map is epic, use [lem-weil-pbc-site-abelian-sheaf-epi-locally-surjective] and the exact forgetful functor of the module-colimits node. Sectionwise kernels prove left exactness. Hence the inverse-limit sequence is short exact. Finally localization is the filtered colimit of repeated multiplication by $\ell$; [lem-weil-pbc-site-abelian-sheaves-filtered-colimits-exact] and the same exact colimit-preserving forgetful functor show it preserves this short exact sequence. The normalization and naturality of steps 1–3 identify it with the image under $J_T$ of the original exact representation sequence.

source.place: Proof of Corollary 6.8.5, with exact products and repleteness expanded; filtered colimits: Stacks Tag 03CO, module limits and forgetful: 03DA,03DB

proof.text: Obtaining connected qcqs topologically Noetherian charts. For each of the finitely many given objects use [lem-weil-pbc-lisse-lattice-etale-local] to obtain an etale covering with integral lisse lattices. Iterating these coverings for the finitely many objects gives a common covering in the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]; existing lattices restrict to later stages. On an etale slice the continuous-function coefficient rings are literally the coefficient rings of that slice, by [def-weil-pbc-lisse-lattice-coefficients], so restricting preserves the finite free local models and the rationalization isomorphisms. Refine each member by affine neighbourhoods mapping into affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $S$. Since an etale map is locally of finite presentation [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], these can be chosen $\operatorname{Spec}B$ with $B$ a finitely presented, in particular finitely generated, $R$-algebra. The open $\operatorname{Spec}R$ has Noetherian underlying space, so [lem-sfb-finite-type-noetherian-spectrum] gives the same property for $\operatorname{Spec}B$. By [lem-sc-noetherian-finite-irreducible-components] it has finitely many irreducible components. Form the finite graph joining two components when they meet. The union in each graph component is connected (a chain of intersecting connected irreducible sets), closed (a finite union of closed sets), and open (its complementary graph components also have closed union). These unions partition the chart and are precisely its connected components. Each is a connected open subscheme with Noetherian underlying space, hence qcqs: every open subset is quasi-compact. Indeed, finite unions from any open covering have a maximal member by the ascending chain condition; adjoining any remaining covering open shows this member covers the subset. This applies to the whole scheme and every intersection of two affine opens. They still form an etale covering of $S$. Discard empty members. Choose a point in each nonempty member and an algebraic closure of its residue field by [def-weil-algebraic-closure]; this gives the required geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point]. This step uses no ring-theoretic Noetherianity or separation of $S$.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(6), connected refinement in Corollary 6.8.5; Stacks Topology Tag 0052 (lemma-Noetherian); finite type spectrum input explicitly separated

proof.text: Realizing the whole finite diagram. On a member $T_i$ of step 6 let $M_{a,i}$ be the integral lattice of each pulled-back object. The equivalence of step 1 writes it as $K_{T_i}(B_{a,i})$. Tensoring $B_{a,i}$ with $E$ gives $V_{a,i}$ with continuous action: its action matrix has continuous entries on the invariant lattice, hence on the same finite dimensional vector space. The normalization of step 3 identifies $J_{T_i}(V_{a,i})$ with $M_{a,i}[1/\ell]$ and with $u_i^{-1}L_a$. Write $\iota_{a,i}:J_{T_i}(V_{a,i})\xrightarrow{\sim}u_i^{-1}L_a$ for these isomorphisms. For an arrow $b:a\to c$, full faithfulness in step 3 gives a unique equivariant $E$-linear map $h_{b,i}$ satisfying $J_{T_i}(h_{b,i})=\iota_{c,i}^{-1}\circ u_i^{-1}f_b\circ\iota_{a,i}$. For two composable arrows the middle factors $\iota_{c,i}\circ\iota_{c,i}^{-1}$ cancel, so applying $J_{T_i}$ to their composite gives precisely the conjugate of the composite sheaf arrow. The identity arrow gives the identity map by the same formula. Faithfulness then reflects every stipulated equality of paths in the diagram. It is unnecessary to arrange integral preservation of all of the chosen lattices by all arrows: the Hom localization has already proved the assertion for rational maps. If there are no objects choose the same connected refinement of $S$ without invoking lattice covers; if $S$ is empty choose the empty covering. Thus the construction covers empty diagrams, rank zero, and the empty base.

It adds no ell-invertibility, ring-Noetherian or separation hypothesis, and it gives the parent exactly what its step 2 uses. Step 2: checked the hypotheses of det-pe-bounded-continuity-sections (qcqs T, filtered N, degree 0, q=0); this is the BS 6.8.4(4) argument. Step 3: stable lattice for compact Pi; clearing denominators and lattice independence are written out. Step 4: B∩V' is finitely generated by ACC before freeness is applied; the A-linear splitting gives exact reductions (tested on a split two-dimensional case and on V'=V). Step 5: the product-exactness, Milnor and lift-defect-correction argument is correct, and localization is an exact filtered colimit. Step 6: the finite-presentation chart over affine Spec R, the Noetherian-spectrum lemma, finitely many irreducible components, clopen connected pieces and qcqs are all checked. Step 7: correctly elementary. New node lem-sfb-integral-lisse-reduction-equivalence: this is BS 6.8.4(1) ('left to the reader') with the 6.8.2 identities. It is true and strictly smaller than the item. I read every DAG node citing 6.8.4 and none is a duplicate.
